result.title: Where It Breaks: Diagnosing Perception, Memory, and Decision Failures of a Vision-Language Agent in Pac-Man
result.summary: Training an agent to play Pac-Man with only up, down, left and right actions raises a basic question: when performance is poor, what should be improved? Difficulty can arise from reading the screen or from choosing actions over a long sequence. We examine these problems in a Qwen3.5-9B-based agent through separate perception checks and primitive-policy reinforcement-learning studies. In the policy study, which uses textual boards to remove image transcription from the decision interface, completion on eight held-out mazes increased from 0% before this optimization to 80.2% at a selected checkpoint, with three extra lives. The perception checks show that accurate static screenshot reading can coexist with errors during interaction. A separate policy comparison also shows that further optimization can accompany worse action choices. Together, these findings motivate concrete checks for post-training: evaluate perception in use, distinguish training success from full-game validation, and examine decisions and later performance rather than relying on one selected score. The study provides empirical lessons for improving future agent training and evaluation.

AI.brief_summary: 论文以 Qwen3.5-9B 驱动的 Pac-Man agent 为对象，通过静态截图感知检查与纯文本棋盘上的策略强化学习实验，分离并诊断感知、长程记忆和动作决策各自的失败。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「感知在交互中是否真的可用」及训练成功与整局验证脱节的发现，直接关联 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、状态保留和评估设计；可供核查其诊断方法，但任务为游戏智能体而非 latent 生成。
